problem: Part (f) asks for the deceleration that removes the 5 m/s closing speed over the 12 s time-to-zero-gap. The arithmetic 5 ÷ 12 = 0.42 m/s² is right, but the answer reads as if 0.42 m/s² were the deceleration the ACC must produce. It is only the deceleration that brings the closing speed to zero at 12 s, when 30 m of gap are left. A student can wrongly conclude this is the minimum needed to stay safe. The minimum relative deceleration to stop the gap reaching zero is a = closing² ÷ (2d) = 5² ÷ (2 × 60) ≈ 0.21 m/s². To fall back to the 50 m target gap, the host must lose 5 m/s over 10 m, i.e. 5² ÷ (2 × 10) = 1.25 m/s².
fix: Keep 0.42 m/s² but label it clearly as 'the relative deceleration that brings the closing speed to zero exactly when the gap would otherwise have closed to zero; many smaller values also avoid contact'. Add one line: the minimum relative deceleration to just avoid contact is closing² ÷ (2d) ≈ 0.21 m/s², and the value the ACC actually aims for is the one that brings the gap down to d_target, here about 1.25 m/s².

problem: 'COAST lowers the stored speed without using the pedal' is vague. On most cars COAST closes the throttle and lets the car slow while the button is held; the lower speed is stored as the new v_set only when the button is released. As written, a student may think COAST directly edits v_set without any vehicle deceleration.
fix: Write: 'COAST (SET− on many cars) closes the throttle and lets the car slow while it is held; when released, the present lower speed becomes the new v_set. It works without the driver touching the pedal.'

problem: Kp and Ki are named but no units are given, while e is in m/s and u in %. A student cannot check the units of each term.
fix: Add: 'Kp is in % per (m/s); Ki is in % per (m/s) per second' (or state that gains are in whatever units make u come out as %).

problem: 'picks the nearest car in the host lane with the smallest time gap' reads like two separate tests. For one host speed the nearest car in the lane is the smallest time gap, so the phrasing can confuse.
fix: Write: 'Target selection picks the closest car in the host lane, which is also the one with the smallest time gap; the camera helps identify lanes.'
